exposure to high fat (fat rich) diet during different stages of pregnancy has different effects on the developing fetus and that these effects may influence future risk for developing MetS later on in life.

understanding the mechanisms of fetal adaptations to a high fat maternal diet that may predispose the fetus to Metabolic Syndrome in later life.
the effects of maternal obesity on the development of Metabolic Syndrome (Mets) in the offspring.
the effects of a maternal high fat (HF; 35.5%) diet on the developing fetus and the mechanisms by which this exposure leads to the development of Metabolic Syndrome (MS) in the offspring.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are critical windows of vulnerability during gestation in mice that are associated with exposure to a HF maternal diet.
the critical periods of increased fetal susceptibility to maternal high fat diet include the periconceptional period and the midgestation period.
the critical period during which a high fat diet has the greatest impact on the fetus is during mid-gestation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
maternal exposure to a HF during pregnancy can alter the expression of hepatic genes in the fetus that may predispose the fetus to future development of MetS.
there are critical windows during gestation in the fetal life that can be shaped by maternal nutrition.
maternal exposure to HF during midpregnancy leads to fetal adaptations that may predispose the offspring to Metabolic Syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are critical windows of time during gestation in the mouse that the fetus is actively being shaped by its environment and the maternal diet.
there are critical windows of development in which the fetus may be particularly sensitive to environmental factors.
the fetus is not a passive passenger, but is actively shaped by its environment during gestation.
